# Root Native Web: full documentation

> Every page of the docs site, in sidebar order. scripts/build-llms.mjs generates this file
> from docs/docs. Don't edit it by hand.

Docs: https://rootnative.github.io/web/
Source: https://github.com/rootnative/web

---

# Root Native Web

`@rootnative/web` is a standalone web runtime for React Native apps. You write `react-native`. It runs in the browser as a real web app.

> **WARNING: Early alpha**
>
> The API can still change between releases. Each page lists what ships today and what doesn't.

## Why

[react-native-web](https://github.com/necolas/react-native-web) tracks React Native and stops there. This project starts from the browser and asks a different question: what does a React Native app need to be a good web app?

- **Parity first.** Every `react-native` export that ships behaves as it does on iOS and Android.
- **Web second, behind the same API.** Semantic HTML, SEO, server rendering, DOM events, logical CSS properties, and the browser features that native doesn't have.
- **Modern only.** TypeScript, ESM, React 19. No Flow, no CommonJS, no `findDOMNode`, no `forwardRef`.

## How it works

Your app imports `react-native`. The [Vite plugin](https://rootnative.github.io/web/vite-plugin) resolves that name to `@rootnative/web`. Your app code uses three entry points:

| Layer  | Import                   | What's in it                                                    |
| ------ | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Parity | `@rootnative/web`        | The React Native components and APIs                            |
| Web    | `@rootnative/web/dom`    | Browser features that native doesn't have, for example `<Head>` |
| Server | `@rootnative/web/server` | Server rendering helpers                                        |

Import `@rootnative/web/dom` and `@rootnative/web/server` only in code that runs on the web. The rest of your app stays the same code that runs on iOS and Android. A fourth entry, `@rootnative/web/vite`, is the Vite plugin, for `vite.config.ts` only.

## Next steps

- [Installation](https://rootnative.github.io/web/installation): set up a Vite app in four steps.
- [Status](https://rootnative.github.io/web/status): what ships today, what's planned, and how it's tested.

---

# Installation

You need React 19 and React DOM 19. This page uses Vite 8 and the package's Vite plugin. For another bundler, see [Without the plugin](https://rootnative.github.io/web/vite-plugin#without-the-plugin).

## Install the package

```bash
npm install @rootnative/web
```

React and React DOM are peer dependencies. A Vite React app has them already.

## Add the Vite plugin

Your app imports `react-native`. The plugin resolves that name to `@rootnative/web`:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { rootnative } from '@rootnative/web/vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), rootnative()],
})
```

It also resolves `.web.tsx` files first, defines `__DEV__`, and puts `'web'` in place of `Platform.OS`. See [Vite plugin](https://rootnative.github.io/web/vite-plugin).

## Add the types

TypeScript needs the same mapping. Add a declaration file to a folder that your `tsconfig.json` includes, for example `src/`:

```ts title="src/react-native.d.ts"
declare module 'react-native' {
  export * from '@rootnative/web'
}
```

Keep this file free of top-level `import` and `export` lines. With one, the declaration stops working, and TypeScript reports `Cannot find module 'react-native'`.

The file also gives you the type of `__DEV__`.

If your app has `.web.tsx` files, tell TypeScript to look for them first:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "moduleSuffixes": [".web", ""]
  }
}
```

Keep the empty string. Without it, TypeScript finds only the `.web` files.

## Mount your app

A React Native app expects a root view that fills the screen. Give the page a full-height root element that lays out its child as flex:

```html title="index.html"
<style>
  html,
  body,
  #root {
    height: 100%;
    margin: 0;
  }
  #root {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: column;
  }
</style>
<div id="root"></div>
```

Then render your app into it with React DOM:

```tsx title="src/main.tsx"
import { StrictMode } from 'react'
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

import { App } from './App'

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App />
  </StrictMode>,
)
```

Now `flex: 1` on your root view fills the window, as it does on iOS and Android:

```tsx title="src/App.tsx"
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native'

export function App() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.screen}>
      <Text style={styles.title}>Hello from React Native</Text>
    </View>
  )
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  screen: { flex: 1, alignItems: 'center', justifyContent: 'center' },
  title: { fontSize: 24 },
})
```

## Browser support

The package targets Chrome 95, Edge 95, Firefox 93, Safari 15.1, and iOS Safari 15.1. Where an older browser lacks a feature, the package uses a fallback.

See [Status](https://rootnative.github.io/web/status) for what ships today and how it's tested.

---

# Vite plugin

`rootnative()` from `@rootnative/web/vite` sets up Vite 8 for a React Native app. It takes no options.

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import { rootnative } from '@rootnative/web/vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), rootnative()],
})
```

## What it does

| Part                 | What it does                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `react-native` alias | Resolves the import name `react-native` to `@rootnative/web`. Only the exact name: a deep import such as `react-native/Libraries/Image` doesn't resolve.                                |
| `.web` files         | Resolves `Button.web.tsx` before `Button.tsx` for an import of `./Button`, as Metro does for the web. Each extension gets a `.web` variant in front.                                    |
| `__DEV__`            | Defines the React Native global: `true` on the dev server, `false` in a production build. It follows `NODE_ENV`, as React's development mode does. Pre-bundled dependencies get it too. |
| `Platform.OS`        | Puts `'web'` in place of each `Platform.OS` read, so the minifier drops the code of the other platforms.                                                                                |

Your own config wins. A `react-native` alias or a `__DEV__` define in your config keeps its value. A `resolve.extensions` list of your own gets the `.web` variants in front.

TypeScript doesn't read the Vite config. For `.web` files, add `moduleSuffixes` to `tsconfig.json`, as [Installation](https://rootnative.github.io/web/installation#add-the-types) shows.

## `Platform.OS`

The plugin changes a read of `Platform.OS` when `Platform` comes from `react-native` or `@rootnative/web`. Named, renamed, and namespace imports all count:

```tsx
import { Platform } from 'react-native'

const label = Platform.OS === 'ios' ? 'iPhone' : 'Web'
// The build sees 'web' === 'ios', so only 'Web' stays in the bundle.
```

At run time `Platform.OS` is `'web'` anyway, so only the bundle size changes. Some reads keep their code, for example when a local variable in the same file has the name `Platform`. On the dev server, pre-bundled dependencies keep their reads too. `Platform.select` keeps its code.

## Server rendering

With Vite's server rendering, the plugin applies to your app code on the server too.

Vite leaves most dependencies to Node, and Node doesn't get the `__DEV__` define. A dependency that reads `__DEV__` then throws a `ReferenceError` on the server. Add that dependency to `ssr.noExternal`, so that Vite transforms it:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), rootnative()],
  ssr: { noExternal: ['some-library'] },
})
```

## Without the plugin

With another bundler, or without the plugin, set up the alias, the `.web` extensions, and `__DEV__` yourself. In Vite:

```ts title="vite.config.ts"
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

const extensions = ['.mjs', '.js', '.mts', '.ts', '.jsx', '.tsx', '.json']
const dev = JSON.stringify(process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production')

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  resolve: {
    alias: [{ find: /^react-native$/, replacement: '@rootnative/web' }],
    extensions: [...extensions.map((extension) => `.web${extension}`), ...extensions],
  },
  define: { __DEV__: dev },
  // The dependency optimizer doesn't apply `define`, so pre-bundled libraries need their own.
  optimizeDeps: { rolldownOptions: { transform: { define: { __DEV__: dev } } } },
})
```

`Platform.OS` then stays a read at run time. It still returns `'web'`.

---

# Status

`@rootnative/web` is in early alpha. The API can change between alpha releases. This page lists what exists, so nothing on this site reads as a promise.

The latest release is [`0.0.0-alpha.1`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rootnative/web) on npm. The [changelog](https://github.com/rootnative/web/blob/main/packages/web/CHANGELOG.md) lists the changes in each release.

## What ships today

| Group      | Exports                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Components | [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view), [`Text`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/text), [`Image`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/image), [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable), [`TouchableHighlight`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablehighlight), [`TouchableNativeFeedback`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablenativefeedback), [`TouchableOpacity`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchableopacity), [`TouchableWithoutFeedback`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablewithoutfeedback), [`Button`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/button), [`ScrollView`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/scrollview), [`FlatList`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/flatlist), [`TextInput`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/textinput), [`Switch`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/switch), [`ActivityIndicator`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/activityindicator), [`StatusBar`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/statusbar) |
| APIs       | [`StyleSheet`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/stylesheet), [`Platform`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/platform), [`Dimensions`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/dimensions), [`useWindowDimensions`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/dimensions), [`Appearance`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/appearance), [`useColorScheme`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/appearance), [`AccessibilityInfo`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/accessibilityinfo), [`I18nManager`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/i18nmanager), [`BackHandler`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/backhandler), [`PixelRatio`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pixelratio), [`processColor`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/processcolor), [`PanResponder`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/panresponder), [`usePressability`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/usepressability)                                                  |
| Web layer  | [`Head`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/seo), from `@rootnative/web/dom`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Server     | `createStyleRegistry`, `StyleRegistryProvider`, `renderStyleTags`, `styleTagsHTML`, `StyleRegistry`, from `@rootnative/web/server`. See [Server rendering](https://rootnative.github.io/web/server-rendering).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Tooling    | [`rootnative()`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/vite-plugin), the Vite plugin, from `@rootnative/web/vite`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

`FlatList` renders every item. It has no virtualizer yet, so keep long lists short for now.

## Planned, not written

**Don't import these yet.** They aren't in the package.

- **Components:** `RefreshControl`, `Modal`.
- **APIs:** `Alert`, `AppState`, `Linking`, `Share`, `Vibration`, `Clipboard`.
- **Lists and motion:** a virtualizer for `FlatList`, `SectionList`, `VirtualizedList`, `Animated`, and `LayoutAnimation`.
- **Tooling:** a Next.js plugin, and templates for a Vite app with and without server rendering.

## Out of scope

- The `react-native-web` internals and file layout.
- Expo and Metro. A Metro plugin isn't planned for 1.0.
- React 18, CommonJS, and Flow.
- Props that React Native doesn't have, except a small web-only set. Each page marks a web-only prop.

## How it's tested

Every component and API has tests. They run in a real Chromium browser through Vitest browser mode, not in a simulated DOM.

Firefox and Safari aren't in the test run yet.

---

# Semantic HTML

The `role` prop picks the HTML element. You don't need a web-only component or a web-only prop.

```tsx
<View role="main">
  <View role="navigation" />
  <Text role="heading" aria-level={1}>
    Title
  </Text>
  <View role="list">
    <View role="listitem">
      <Text>One</Text>
    </View>
  </View>
  <Text href="/about" role="link">
    About
  </Text>
</View>
```

```html
<main>
  <nav></nav>
  <h1>Title</h1>
  <ul>
    <li><span>One</span></li>
  </ul>
  <a href="/about">About</a>
</main>
```

Screen readers, search engines, and browser features such as reader mode get the same structure that native accessibility tools get.

## Roles that pick an element

| `role`             | Element                                                       |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `article`          | `<article>`                                                   |
| `banner`           | `<header>`                                                    |
| `button`           | `<button type="button">`, so it never submits a form          |
| `complementary`    | `<aside>`                                                     |
| `contentinfo`      | `<footer>`                                                    |
| `figure`           | `<figure>`                                                    |
| `form`             | `<form>`                                                      |
| `heading`          | `<h1>` to `<h6>`, from `aria-level`. The default level is 2.  |
| `link` with `href` | `<a>`                                                         |
| `list`             | `<ul>`                                                        |
| `listitem`         | `<li>`                                                        |
| `main`             | `<main>`                                                      |
| `navigation`       | `<nav>`                                                       |
| `separator`        | `<hr>`. A separator with children is a `<div>` with the role. |

Every other role keeps the default element, `<div>` for `View` and `<span>` for `Text`, with a `role` attribute.

The table roles (`table`, `row`, `cell`, and the others) also stay on a `<div>` with the ARIA role. A real `<table>` would let the HTML parser move elements around, so the server HTML wouldn't match the React tree, and flex layout wouldn't apply.

## Links

`href` on a `View` or a `Text` renders an `<a>`. You don't need `role="link"` with it. On a `Text`, `target`, `rel`, and `download` pass to the anchor too. These props are web only.

`role="link"` without `href` keeps the default element and adds `role="link"`.

## `accessibilityRole`

`accessibilityRole` works too. When you set both, `role` wins. The older names map to their ARIA roles:

| `accessibilityRole`   | Role        |
| --------------------- | ----------- |
| `header`              | `heading`   |
| `image`               | `img`       |
| `imagebutton`         | `button`    |
| `summary`             | `region`    |
| `adjustable`          | `slider`    |
| `search`              | `searchbox` |
| `text`, `keyboardkey` | `none`      |

## Accessibility props

The React Native accessibility props become ARIA attributes:

| Prop                                                                             | Attribute                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `accessibilityLabel`                                                             | `aria-label`                                                                   |
| `accessibilityLabelledBy`                                                        | `aria-labelledby`. An array joins with spaces.                                 |
| `accessibilityHint`                                                              | `aria-description`                                                             |
| `accessibilityLiveRegion`                                                        | `aria-live`. `none` is `off`.                                                  |
| `accessibilityState`                                                             | `aria-busy`, `aria-checked`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected` |
| `accessibilityValue`                                                             | `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuetext`            |
| `accessibilityViewIsModal`                                                       | `aria-modal`                                                                   |
| `accessibilityElementsHidden`, `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` | `aria-hidden`                                                                  |
| `nativeID`, `id`                                                                 | `id`                                                                           |
| `testID`                                                                         | `data-testid`                                                                  |
| `focusable`                                                                      | `tabIndex` 0, or -1 for `false`. `tabIndex` wins when you set both.            |

`aria-*` props pass through as you write them. An `aria-*` prop wins over the mapped prop with the same meaning.

`data-*` props pass through too. Any other prop that isn't a React Native prop is dropped, so it never reaches the element.

---

# Styles

You style with the `style` prop and `StyleSheet.create`, as on native. At runtime, each declaration becomes one atomic CSS class, and every element with the same declaration shares that class.

```tsx
const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: { padding: 16, borderRadius: 12, backgroundColor: '#fff' },
})
```

Prefer `StyleSheet.create` for static styles. Its objects are frozen, so their class names compile once. An inline style object compiles again on each render.

## Defaults

Every `View` starts with the React Native defaults: `display: flex`, `flexDirection: 'column'`, `alignItems: 'stretch'`, `flexShrink: 0`, `position: 'relative'`, and a border box.

Every `Text` starts at 14 px, black, in the system font, and keeps its spaces and line breaks.

## Values

- **Numbers get `px`.** `padding: 16` is `16px`, and `lineHeight: 20` is `20px`, as on native. `flex`, `flexGrow`, `flexShrink`, `opacity`, `zIndex`, `aspectRatio`, and `fontWeight` stay unitless.
- **Strings pass through.** `'50%'` and `'auto'` work as they do on native.
- **Colors use the React Native parser.** Named colors, hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()`, and `hwb()` all work. A color that React Native can't parse is dropped.

## Flex

`flex` follows the React Native rules, not the CSS ones:

| Value      | CSS        | Meaning                                        |
| ---------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `flex: 1`  | `1 1 0%`   | Grow and shrink, from a size of 0              |
| `flex: 0`  | `0 0 auto` | Keep the size of the content                   |
| `flex: -1` | `0 1 auto` | Keep the size of the content, shrink if needed |

`gap`, `inset`, `display: 'contents'`, and `position: 'static'` pass through to CSS.

## Shorthands and longhands

A longhand always wins over a shorthand, whatever the key order, as on native:

```tsx
// The top padding is 16. The other three sides are 8.
const styles = StyleSheet.create({ box: { paddingTop: 16, padding: 8 } })
```

## Right-to-left

The start and end props map to CSS logical properties, so the browser flips them when the page direction is right-to-left:

| Prop                                                                                             | CSS                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
| `marginStart`, `marginEnd`, `paddingStart`, `paddingEnd`                                         | `margin-inline-start` and the others       |
| `start`, `end`                                                                                   | `inset-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`   |
| `borderStartWidth`, `borderEndWidth`, `borderStartColor`, `borderEndColor`                       | `border-inline-start-width` and the others |
| `borderTopStartRadius`, `borderTopEndRadius`, `borderBottomStartRadius`, `borderBottomEndRadius` | `border-start-start-radius` and the others |

`marginHorizontal` and `paddingHorizontal` set the left and right sides, as on native.

`marginLeft`, `paddingLeft`, `left`, and their right partners stay on the physical side in a right-to-left layout. On native they swap by default. Use the start and end props for anything that must follow the direction. See [`I18nManager`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/i18nmanager#left-and-right-styles).

## Transforms, shadows, and filters

- **`transform`** takes the React Native array, for example `[{ translateX: 10 }, { rotate: '45deg' }]`, or a CSS string. `transformOrigin` works too.
- **`boxShadow`** takes the React Native object array or a CSS string.
- **`shadowColor`, `shadowOffset`, `shadowOpacity`, `shadowRadius`** become a `box-shadow` when you don't set `boxShadow`.
- **`textShadowColor`, `textShadowOffset`, `textShadowRadius`** become a `text-shadow`.
- **`filter`** takes the React Native array, for example `[{ blur: 4 }]`, or a CSS string.

## Fonts

- `fontFamily: 'System'` is the system font stack of the browser.
- The named weights (`'thin'`, `'light'`, `'medium'`, `'semibold'`, `'heavy'`, `'black'`, and the others) become their numbers.
- `fontVariant` takes the React Native array.

## Native-only style props

`elevation`, `borderCurve`, `includeFontPadding`, and `overlayColor` have no web effect. The package accepts them and ignores them.

---

# Server rendering

The server renders your app to HTML with React DOM. A style registry collects the CSS of that render, and you write it into `<head>`. The browser then hydrates the same app.

## On the server

Render the whole document with React, not only the app:

```tsx title="server.tsx"
import { renderToString } from 'react-dom/server'
import { createStyleRegistry, StyleRegistryProvider, styleTagsHTML } from '@rootnative/web/server'

import { App } from './App'

export function renderPage(): string {
  const registry = createStyleRegistry()
  const html = renderToString(
    <html lang="en">
      <head>
        <meta charSet="utf-8" />
        <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
      </head>
      <body>
        <div id="root">
          <StyleRegistryProvider registry={registry}>
            <App />
          </StyleRegistryProvider>
        </div>
        <script type="module" src="/client.js" />
      </body>
    </html>,
  )
  return `<!doctype html>${html.replace('</head>', `${styleTagsHTML(registry)}</head>`)}`
}
```

The script path depends on your bundler. Put the root CSS from [Installation](https://rootnative.github.io/web/installation#mount-your-app) in the head too.

Three rules:

- **One registry per request.** A shared registry mixes the CSS of two requests.
- **Write the style tags after the render ends.** The registry fills while React renders. A head that you send before the body renders misses the CSS of that body.
- **Render the `<head>` with React.** React 19 puts the `<title>` and `<meta>` elements of [`Head`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/seo) into the `<head>` that it renders. If you render only the app and paste it into a template, they land at the start of `<body>`.

Your server code needs the same setup, so that `App` and its imports resolve to `@rootnative/web`. With Vite's server rendering, the [Vite plugin](https://rootnative.github.io/web/vite-plugin#server-rendering) does it.

`renderStyleTags(registry)` returns the same two `<style>` elements as React elements. Use it when your framework takes head elements, not a string.

## In the browser

Hydrate the same app into the same element:

```tsx title="client.tsx"
import { hydrateRoot } from 'react-dom/client'

import { App } from './App'

hydrateRoot(document.getElementById('root')!, <App />)
```

The client needs no provider. It finds the two `<style>` elements by their id and adopts their rules, so it inserts no rule twice.

## Values that differ on the server

The server doesn't know the window or the user's settings. Two hooks return a fixed value on the server and during hydration, so the first client render matches the server HTML. The real value arrives right after hydration.

| Hook                    | On the server and during hydration                |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `useWindowDimensions()` | `{ width: 0, height: 0, scale: 1, fontScale: 1 }` |
| `useColorScheme()`      | `'light'`                                         |

In render, use these hooks, not `Dimensions.get()` or `Appearance.getColorScheme()`. The two getters return the fixed value on the server but the real value in the browser at once, so a render that reads them doesn't match the server HTML.

A layout that depends on the window width renders its zero-width branch first. Use flex and percentages for the first paint, and refine after hydration.

---

# SEO

`Head` sets the title and the meta tags of a page. React 19 moves them into `<head>`, on the server and in the browser.

```tsx
import { Head } from '@rootnative/web/dom'

export function ArticleScreen() {
  return (
    <View role="main">
      <Head
        title="Page title"
        description="What the page is about"
        canonical="https://example.com/page"
        openGraph={{ title: 'Page title', image: 'https://example.com/og.png' }}
        jsonLd={{ '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'WebPage', name: 'Page title' }}
      />
      {/* The page */}
    </View>
  )
}
```

`Head` is in the web layer. Import it only in code that runs on the web.

## Props

| Prop          | Renders                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `title`       | `<title>`                                                                                               |
| `description` | `<meta name="description">`                                                                             |
| `canonical`   | `<link rel="canonical">`                                                                                |
| `robots`      | `<meta name="robots">`, for example `"noindex"`                                                         |
| `themeColor`  | `<meta name="theme-color">`                                                                             |
| `openGraph`   | One `<meta property="og:…">` for each of `title`, `description`, `image`, `url`, `type`, and `siteName` |
| `jsonLd`      | `<script type="application/ld+json">`, from one schema.org object or an array of them                   |
| `children`    | Extra `<meta>`, `<link>`, and `<title>` elements                                                        |

Use `children` for a tag that has no prop, for example a Twitter card:

```tsx
<Head title="Page title">
  <meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image" />
</Head>
```

## Rules

- **Use one `Head` per page.** React doesn't merge two of them.
- **A `Head` leaves with its screen.** Its elements go away when it unmounts, so the next screen's `Head` starts clean.
- **The JSON-LD script stays where `Head` renders,** in the body. Search engines read JSON-LD there too. A `<` in the data is escaped, so a string can't close the script.
- **Set the theme color in one place.** `themeColor` and the `backgroundColor` of `StatusBar` write the same meta tag.
- **On the server, render the `<head>` with React,** so the tags land in it. See [Server rendering](https://rootnative.github.io/web/server-rendering).

---

# `View`

The basic container. It renders a `<div>`, or the element that its [`role`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/semantic-html) picks, with the React Native layout defaults.

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, View } from 'react-native'

export function Toolbar({ children }) {
  return (
    <View role="navigation" style={styles.toolbar}>
      {children}
    </View>
  )
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  toolbar: { flexDirection: 'row', gap: 8, padding: 12 },
})
```

## Props

| Prop                                                   | On the web                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `style`                                                | Compiles to atomic CSS. See [Styles](https://rootnative.github.io/web/styles).                                                                                                                  |
| `role`, `accessibilityRole`                            | Picks the element. See [Semantic HTML](https://rootnative.github.io/web/semantic-html).                                                                                                         |
| `accessibilityLabel` and the other accessibility props | Become ARIA attributes. See [Accessibility props](https://rootnative.github.io/web/semantic-html#accessibility-props).                                                                          |
| `onLayout`                                             | Fires after mount and after each size change, from a `ResizeObserver`. `x` and `y` are relative to the parent view. A move with no size change doesn't fire it. |
| `pointerEvents`                                        | `none`, `auto`, `box-none`, and `box-only`, as on native.                                                                                                       |
| `focusable`, `tabIndex`                                | `focusable` sets `tabIndex` to 0, or to -1 for `false`. `tabIndex` wins when you set both.                                                                      |
| `nativeID`, `id`, `testID`                             | `id`, `id`, and `data-testid`.                                                                                                                                  |
| `href`                                                 | **Web only.** Renders an `<a>`.                                                                                                                                 |
| `aria-level`                                           | **Web only.** The heading level of `role="heading"`, 1 to 6.                                                                                                    |
| `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, and the other DOM handlers     | **Web only.** Every React DOM event handler passes to the element.                                                                                              |
| `collapsable`, `accessible`                            | Accepted and ignored.                                                                                                                                           |

Any other prop that isn't a React Native prop is dropped.

## Ref

The ref is the DOM element. The native methods `measure`, `measureInWindow`, `measureLayout`, and `setNativeProps` aren't there. Use `onLayout`, or call `getBoundingClientRect()` on the element.

---

# `Text`

Renders text in a `<span>`, or the element that its [`role`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/semantic-html) picks.

```tsx
import { Text } from 'react-native'

export function Byline({ author }) {
  return (
    <Text numberOfLines={1}>
      By <Text style={{ fontWeight: 'bold' }}>{author}</Text>
    </Text>
  )
}
```

A `Text` starts at 14 px, black, in the system font, and keeps its spaces and line breaks, as on native. A `Text` inside a `Text` takes the font, color, alignment, and decoration of its parent.

## Props

| Prop                                 | On the web                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `style`                              | Compiles to atomic CSS. See [Styles](https://rootnative.github.io/web/styles).                                                                                    |
| `numberOfLines`                      | `1` keeps the text on one line and ends it with an ellipsis. A larger number clamps the text to that many lines.                  |
| `ellipsizeMode`                      | `tail` (the default) and `clip`. `head` and `middle` show the ellipsis at the end for now.                                        |
| `selectable`                         | The text is selectable by default, as web users expect. On native the default is `false`. `false` turns selection off.            |
| `selectionColor`                     | The background color of selected text.                                                                                            |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut` | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable#how-a-press-works): a pointer, Enter or Space, or a click. The event is a `GestureResponderEvent`. |
| `onLongPress`                        | A press held for 500 ms. `onPress` then doesn't fire.                                                                             |
| `pressRetentionOffset`               | How far a pointer can leave the text and still press it, as on `Pressable`.                                                       |
| `suppressHighlighting`               | Ignored, as on Android. Only iOS highlights a pressed `Text`.                                                                     |
| `disabled`                           | Sets `aria-disabled`. The `Text` isn't pressable, so a pressable parent gets the press.                                           |
| `role`, accessibility props          | See [Semantic HTML](https://rootnative.github.io/web/semantic-html).                                                                                              |
| `onLayout`, `pointerEvents`          | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                                                            |
| `nativeID`, `id`, `testID`           | `id`, `id`, and `data-testid`.                                                                                                    |
| `href`                               | **Web only.** Renders an `<a>`.                                                                                                   |
| `target`, `rel`, `download`          | **Web only.** Pass to the anchor.                                                                                                 |
| `lang`                               | **Web only.** The language of the text, for screen readers and hyphenation.                                                       |
| `aria-level`                         | **Web only.** The heading level of `role="heading"`, 1 to 6.                                                                      |
| `onClick` and the other DOM handlers | **Web only.** Pass to the element. On a pressable `Text`, they run before the press handlers, and both run.                       |

As on native, only `onPress` or `onLongPress` makes a `Text` pressable. A `Text` with only `onPressIn` or `onPressOut` doesn't respond.

> **NOTE: A pressable text is a link**
>
> As on native, a pressable `Text` with no `role` has the role `link`. It's in the tab order, and Enter or Space presses it. With an `href`, it renders an `<a>`. For an action, set `role="button"`, and it renders a `<button>`.

## Ref

The ref is the DOM element.

---

# `Image`

Shows an image. It renders a box (a `<div>`) with an `<img>` inside. The style sizes the box, and `resizeMode` fits the image in it.

```tsx
import { Image } from 'react-native'

export function Avatar({ url }) {
  return (
    <Image
      source={{ uri: url }}
      style={{ width: 48, height: 48, borderRadius: 24 }}
      accessibilityLabel="Profile photo"
    />
  )
}
```

With no size in the style and no `width` and `height` in the source, the image is 0 × 0, as on native. The box clips the image to its border radius.

## Sources

| `source`                             | On the web                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{ uri }`                            | The `src` of the `<img>`. A `width` and `height` in the source size the box when the style doesn't.                                 |
| An array with `scale` on each entry  | A `srcset` with `x` descriptors. The browser picks the entry for the pixel density of the screen.                                   |
| An array with `width` on each entry  | A `srcset` with `w` descriptors. `sizes` is the style width, or `100vw` when the style has none. The browser picks by layout width. |
| An array with mixed entries          | The first entry, as on Android.                                                                                                     |
| `{ uri, headers }`, `method`, `body` | A `fetch` with the headers, the method, and the body. The `<img>` shows the result.                                                 |
| A string                             | **Web only.** A URL, for example the one that your bundler gives for an imported image file.                                        |
| A number                             | A Metro asset id from `require('./image.png')`. It has no meaning on the web, so the image warns once and loads nothing.            |

To use a local image, import it and pass the URL:

```tsx
import { Image } from 'react-native'

import logo from './logo.png'

export function Logo() {
  return <Image source={logo} style={{ width: 120, height: 40 }} />
}
```

The `src` and `srcSet` props work too, as on native.

## Props

| Prop                                                                                    | On the web                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `resizeMode`                                                                            | `cover` (the default), `contain`, `stretch`, `center`, and `repeat`. `resizeMode` and `objectFit` in the style work too. |
| `tintColor`                                                                             | Paints the color through the shape of the image. The box then carries `role="img"` and the label.                        |
| `blurRadius`                                                                            | A CSS blur.                                                                                                              |
| `defaultSource`                                                                         | Shows until the source loads.                                                                                            |
| `alt`, `accessibilityLabel`                                                             | The text alternative of the image.                                                                                       |
| `onLoadStart`, `onLoad`, `onLoadEnd`, `onError`                                         | As on native. `onLoad` gets `nativeEvent.source` with the `uri`, `width`, and `height`.                                  |
| `onProgress`                                                                            | Never fires. The browser doesn't report progress for an image.                                                           |
| `crossOrigin`, `referrerPolicy`                                                         | Pass to the `<img>`.                                                                                                     |
| `width`, `height`                                                                       | Size the box when the style doesn't.                                                                                     |
| `loading`, `fetchPriority`, `decoding`                                                  | **Web only.** The loading hints of the `<img>`.                                                                          |
| `onLayout`, accessibility props, `nativeID`, `testID`                                   | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                                                   |
| `resizeMethod`, `fadeDuration`, `progressiveRenderingEnabled`, `loadingIndicatorSource` | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                                                       |

With `resizeMode="repeat"` or a `tintColor`, the box paints the image as a CSS background or mask. The `<img>` stays in the box, hidden, so that the load events still fire.

## Statics

| Method                                   | On the web                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Image.getSize(uri)`                     | Loads the image and gives its size. It returns a promise, or calls the success and failure callbacks. |
| `Image.getSizeWithHeaders(uri, headers)` | The same, with a `fetch` that sends the headers.                                                      |
| `Image.prefetch(url)`                    | Loads the image into the browser cache. Resolves `true`.                                              |
| `Image.queryCache(urls)`                 | Resolves `{}`. The browser doesn't show its cache to a page.                                          |
| `Image.resolveAssetSource(source)`       | `{ uri, width, height, scale }` of the source, or `null` for a number.                                |

`getSize` needs a browser. On the server it rejects.

## Ref

The ref is the box element.

---

# `Pressable`

Detects a press, a long press, hover, and focus. It works with a mouse, a pen, touch, and the keyboard, with the press timing of React Native.

```tsx
import { Pressable, StyleSheet, Text } from 'react-native'

export function SaveButton({ onSave }) {
  return (
    <Pressable
      role="button"
      onPress={onSave}
      style={({ pressed, hovered, focused }) => [
        styles.button,
        hovered && styles.hovered,
        pressed && styles.pressed,
        focused && styles.focusRing,
      ]}
    >
      <Text>Save</Text>
    </Pressable>
  )
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  button: { padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: '#e5e7eb' },
  hovered: { backgroundColor: '#d1d5db' },
  pressed: { backgroundColor: '#9ca3af' },
  focusRing: { outlineWidth: 2, outlineStyle: 'solid', outlineColor: '#2563eb' },
})
```

Give an action `role="button"`. It renders a `<button type="button">`, so screen readers announce a button and the browser handles the keyboard. Without a role, `Pressable` renders a focusable `<div>`.

## How a press works

- **Mouse, pen, or touch.** The primary button only. `onPressIn` fires on the pointer down, and `onPress` fires when you release inside the press area. The press area is the element, plus `hitSlop`, plus `pressRetentionOffset`.
- **Keyboard.** Enter or Space, while the `Pressable` has focus. `onPressIn` fires on key down, and `onPress` on key up. Space doesn't scroll the page. With `role="button"`, the browser handles the key, and only `onPress` fires.
- **Assistive technology, or `element.click()`.** `onPress` fires with the click event.
- **Long press.** `onLongPress` fires after `delayLongPress`, 500 ms by default. On a touch screen, a long press with `onLongPress` doesn't open the context menu.
- **Quick taps.** `onPressOut` waits until the press is at least 130 ms long, so a quick tap still shows the pressed style, as on native.

## State

`style` and `children` can be functions of the state:

| Field     | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pressed` | True while a press is down.                                                                                |
| `hovered` | **Web only.** True while a mouse or a pen is over the element. Touch never sets it.                        |
| `focused` | **Web only.** True while the element has keyboard focus, so a focus ring doesn't show after a mouse click. |

As on native, only a `Pressable` whose `style` or `children` is a function renders again when the state changes.

## Props

| Prop                                                               | On the web                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `onLongPress`, `onPressMove` | The event's `nativeEvent` is the DOM event with `locationX`, `locationY`, `pageX`, `pageY`, `timestamp`, `touches`, and `changedTouches` added.                   |
| `onPress`                                                          | Gets the pointer up event. A keyboard or assistive technology press gets the click event. `preventDefault()` on it cancels the click, so a link doesn't navigate. |
| `onHoverIn`, `onHoverOut`, `delayHoverIn`, `delayHoverOut`         | A mouse or a pen. Touch doesn't hover.                                                                                                                            |
| `onFocus`, `onBlur`                                                | Focus events of the element.                                                                                                                                      |
| `disabled`                                                         | Sets `aria-disabled`, takes the element out of the tab order, and stops every press.                                                                              |
| `hitSlop`                                                          | An invisible `::before` box grows the hit area. A parent with `overflow: 'hidden'` clips it.                                                                      |
| `pressRetentionOffset`                                             | How far a pointer can leave the element and still press it. The default is 20 on three sides and 30 at the bottom, as on native.                                  |
| `cancelable`                                                       | `false` sets `touch-action: none`, so a scroll that starts on the element can't cancel the press.                                                                 |
| `unstable_pressDelay`                                              | Delays `onPressIn`.                                                                                                                                               |
| `testOnly_pressed`                                                 | Forces the pressed state.                                                                                                                                         |
| `focusable`                                                        | `false` takes the element out of the tab order.                                                                                                                   |
| `onClick`, `onKeyDown`, and the other DOM handlers                 | **Web only.** Your handler runs first, then the press handling.                                                                                                   |
| View props                                                         | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                                                                                            |
| `android_ripple`, `android_disableSound`, `blockNativeResponder`   | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                                                                                                |

## Ref

The ref is the DOM element.

---

# `TouchableHighlight`

A press target that shows an underlay while you press it. The underlay is a background color, and the child gets a lower opacity on top of it, so the child looks darker. The press handling is the same as on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable#how-a-press-works).

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, TouchableHighlight, View } from 'react-native'

export function Row({ onOpen }) {
  return (
    <TouchableHighlight role="button" underlayColor="#e5e7eb" onPress={onOpen}>
      <View style={styles.row}>
        <Text>Open</Text>
      </View>
    </TouchableHighlight>
  )
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  row: { padding: 16, backgroundColor: 'white' },
})
```

The child must be one element that takes a `style`, for example a `View`. Give the child an opaque background color. The underlay then shows through the child as its opacity drops. Without a child background, the underlay shows at full strength, as on native.

## How the underlay works

- When a press starts, the element gets `underlayColor` as its background, and the child gets `activeOpacity`.
- When the press ends, the underlay goes away. After `onPress`, it stays for `delayPressOut` milliseconds, so a short tap still shows it.
- With no press handler (`onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, or `onLongPress`), there's no underlay.
- The underlay changes render the component again, as on native.

## Props

| Prop                                                                    | On the web                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `underlayColor`                                                         | The background while pressed. The default is black.                                              |
| `activeOpacity`                                                         | The opacity of the child while pressed. The default is `0.85`.                                   |
| `onShowUnderlay`, `onHideUnderlay`                                      | Called when the underlay shows and when it goes away.                                            |
| `testOnly_pressed`                                                      | Shows the underlay all the time.                                                                 |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `onLongPress`                     | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable). There's no minimum press duration, as on native.                |
| `delayPressIn`, `delayPressOut`, `delayLongPress`                       | The press delays, in milliseconds.                                                               |
| `onFocus`, `onBlur`                                                     | Focus events of the element. On native, `TouchableHighlight` doesn't call them.                  |
| `disabled`                                                              | Sets `aria-disabled`, takes the element out of the tab order, and stops every press.             |
| `focusable`                                                             | As on native, the element is in the tab order only with `onPress`. `false` takes it out.         |
| `hitSlop`, `pressRetentionOffset`                                       | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable).                                                                 |
| `rejectResponderTermination`                                            | `true` sets `touch-action: none`, so a scroll that starts on the element can't cancel the press. |
| `onClick` and the other DOM handlers                                    | **Web only.** Your handler runs first, then the press handling.                                  |
| View props                                                              | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                           |
| `touchSoundDisabled`, `hasTVPreferredFocus`, `nextFocusDown` and others | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                               |

## Ref

The ref is the DOM element.

---

# `TouchableNativeFeedback`

On Android, this touchable draws the system ripple. On iOS, React Native shows no feedback, and the press works as on [`TouchableWithoutFeedback`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablewithoutfeedback). The web does the same as iOS.

```tsx
import { Text, TouchableNativeFeedback, View } from 'react-native'

const ripple = TouchableNativeFeedback.Ripple('#2563eb', false)

export function Item({ onOpen }) {
  return (
    <TouchableNativeFeedback role="button" background={ripple} onPress={onOpen}>
      <View>
        <Text>Open</Text>
      </View>
    </TouchableNativeFeedback>
  )
}
```

The child gets the press handlers and the accessibility props, as with [`TouchableWithoutFeedback`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablewithoutfeedback#what-the-child-gets).

## Props

| Prop                                              | On the web                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `background`, `useForeground`                     | Android only. Accepted and ignored, as on iOS.                 |
| The props of `TouchableWithoutFeedback`           | As on [`TouchableWithoutFeedback`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchablewithoutfeedback). |
| `hasTVPreferredFocus`, `nextFocusDown` and others | TV only. Accepted and ignored.                                 |

## Static methods

| Method                                          | On the web                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SelectableBackground(rippleRadius?)`           | Returns the same object as on native, for `background`.                                    |
| `SelectableBackgroundBorderless(rippleRadius?)` | Returns the same object as on native, for `background`.                                    |
| `Ripple(color, borderless, rippleRadius?)`      | Returns the same object as on native, with the color from [`processColor`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/processcolor). |
| `canUseNativeForeground()`                      | `false`, as on iOS.                                                                        |

> **TIP: The React Compiler lint and `Ripple`**
>
> The React Compiler lint reads a capitalized call in a component, such as `TouchableNativeFeedback.Ripple(...)`, as a component, and reports `capitalized-calls`. Make the call once outside the component, as in the example.

---

# `TouchableOpacity`

A press target that dims while you press it. It uses the timing and the curve of React Native, with the same press handling as [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable#how-a-press-works).

```tsx
import { StyleSheet, Text, TouchableOpacity } from 'react-native'

export function SaveButton({ onSave }) {
  return (
    <TouchableOpacity role="button" onPress={onSave} style={styles.button}>
      <Text>Save</Text>
    </TouchableOpacity>
  )
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  button: { padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, backgroundColor: '#e5e7eb' },
})
```

As on `Pressable`, give an action `role="button"`, so it renders a `<button type="button">`. Without a role, it renders a `<div>`.

## How it dims

- When a press starts, the opacity goes to `activeOpacity` at once.
- When the pointer leaves the press area, the opacity goes back over 250 ms. When it comes back, the opacity goes to `activeOpacity` over 150 ms.
- When the press ends, the opacity goes back to the opacity of `style` over 250 ms.
- A change of `disabled` or of the style's opacity also fades to the style's opacity over 250 ms.

The fade uses the Web Animations API, so a press doesn't render the component again. The curve is React Native's `Easing.inOut(Easing.quad)`, as `cubic-bezier(0.455, 0.03, 0.515, 0.955)`.

## Props

| Prop                                                                    | On the web                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `activeOpacity`                                                         | The opacity while pressed. The default is `0.2`.                                                 |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `onLongPress`                     | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable). There's no minimum press duration, as on native.                |
| `delayPressIn`, `delayPressOut`, `delayLongPress`                       | The press delays, in milliseconds.                                                               |
| `onFocus`, `onBlur`                                                     | Focus events of the element. On native, `TouchableOpacity` doesn't call them.                    |
| `disabled`                                                              | Sets `aria-disabled`, takes the element out of the tab order, and stops every press.             |
| `focusable`                                                             | As on native, the element is in the tab order only with `onPress`. `false` takes it out.         |
| `hitSlop`, `pressRetentionOffset`                                       | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable).                                                                 |
| `rejectResponderTermination`                                            | `true` sets `touch-action: none`, so a scroll that starts on the element can't cancel the press. |
| `onClick` and the other DOM handlers                                    | **Web only.** Your handler runs first, then the press handling.                                  |
| View props                                                              | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                           |
| `touchSoundDisabled`, `hasTVPreferredFocus`, `nextFocusDown` and others | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                               |

## Ref

The ref is the DOM element.

---

# `TouchableWithoutFeedback`

Adds press handling to its only child. It renders no element of its own and shows no feedback. The press handling is the same as on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable#how-a-press-works).

```tsx
import { Text, TouchableWithoutFeedback, View } from 'react-native'

export function Card({ onOpen }) {
  return (
    <TouchableWithoutFeedback role="button" onPress={onOpen}>
      <View>
        <Text>Open</Text>
      </View>
    </TouchableWithoutFeedback>
  )
}
```

The child must be one element that passes its props to the DOM, for example a `View` or a `Text`. Your own component works when it passes the props on to a `View`.

## What the child gets

- The press handlers. The child's own DOM handlers run first, for example its `onPointerDown`.
- The accessibility props, `role`, `testID`, `nativeID`, `id`, and `onLayout` of the `TouchableWithoutFeedback`. `style` stays out, as on native.
- `onFocus` and `onBlur` of the `TouchableWithoutFeedback`. Without them, the child keeps its own.
- `focusable`: as on native, the child is in the tab order only with `onPress`, and not when `disabled`.

## Props

| Prop                                                | On the web                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onPress`, `onPressIn`, `onPressOut`, `onLongPress` | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable). There's no minimum press duration, as on native.             |
| `delayPressIn`, `delayPressOut`, `delayLongPress`   | The press delays, in milliseconds.                                                            |
| `disabled`                                          | Sets `aria-disabled` on the child, takes it out of the tab order, and stops every press.      |
| `pressRetentionOffset`                              | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable).                                                              |
| `hitSlop`                                           | The child gets it. A `View` doesn't grow its hit area yet, so it only extends the press area. |
| `rejectResponderTermination`                        | The web ignores it: there's no element of its own to set `touch-action` on.                   |
| `touchSoundDisabled`                                | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                            |

---

# `Button`

A button with a title and a press handler. It renders a `<button type="button">`, so the keyboard and a screen reader see a real button.

```tsx
import { Button } from 'react-native'

export function SaveButton({ onSave }) {
  return <Button title="Save" onPress={onSave} />
}
```

`Button` takes no `style` and no children, as in React Native. For a different look, use [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable) or [`TouchableOpacity`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchableopacity) with `role="button"`.

## How it looks

React Native draws a different button on each platform. The web uses the look of Android:

- A background of `#2196F3`, with a corner radius of 2.
- The title in white, with a weight of 500, centered, with 8 px around it.
- When disabled: a background of `#dfdfdf` and a title of `#a1a1a1`.

Two things differ from Android:

- The title keeps its case. Android makes it uppercase.
- The button has no shadow, because the web ignores `elevation`.

The button dims while you press it, as [`TouchableOpacity`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/touchableopacity#how-it-dims) does.

Inside a `View`, the button takes the full width, as on native. To make it as wide as its title, put it in a `View` with `alignItems: 'flex-start'`.

## Props

| Prop                                                                    | On the web                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`                                                                 | The text of the button. It must be a string, or `Button` throws, as in React Native.                         |
| `onPress`                                                               | As on [`Pressable`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/pressable). Enter and Space press a focused button.                                     |
| `color`                                                                 | The background color, as on Android. On iOS, it's the color of the title.                                    |
| `disabled`                                                              | Sets `aria-disabled`, takes the button out of the tab order, stops the press, and changes the colors.        |
| `accessibilityState`, `aria-disabled`                                   | A `disabled` value in one of them also disables the button. The `disabled` prop wins.                        |
| `accessibilityLabel`, `aria-label`, `accessibilityHint`                 | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                                       |
| `aria-busy`, `aria-checked`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`           | Go to the button.                                                                                            |
| `accessibilityLanguage`                                                 | Sets the `lang` attribute.                                                                                   |
| `importantForAccessibility`                                             | `no` and `no-hide-descendants` set `aria-hidden`, which hides the button and its title from a screen reader. |
| `testID`                                                                | Sets `data-testid`.                                                                                          |
| `accessible`, `accessibilityActions`, `onAccessibilityAction`           | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                                           |
| `touchSoundDisabled`, `hasTVPreferredFocus`, `nextFocusDown` and others | Native only. Accepted and ignored.                                                                           |

## Ref

The ref is the `<button>` element.

---

# `ScrollView`

A box that scrolls on one axis. It renders an overflow `<div>` with your content in a `View` inside.

```tsx
import { ScrollView, Text } from 'react-native'

export function Feed({ posts }) {
  return (
    <ScrollView style={{ flex: 1 }} contentContainerStyle={{ padding: 16, gap: 12 }}>
      {posts.map((post) => (
        <Text key={post.id}>{post.title}</Text>
      ))}
    </ScrollView>
  )
}
```

A `ScrollView` scrolls its own box, not the document. On a phone, the address bar of the browser doesn't hide as you scroll it.

## Scroll events

| Event                                          | On the web                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `onScroll`                                     | One event per frame. `nativeEvent` is the DOM event with `contentOffset`, `contentSize`, `layoutMeasurement`, `contentInset` (zeros), and `zoomScale` (1) added. There's no `velocity`. |
| `onScrollBeginDrag`, `onScrollEndDrag`         | A scroll while a pointer is down is a drag: a finger, or a mouse on the scrollbar. The drag ends when the pointer comes up.                                                             |
| `onMomentumScrollBegin`, `onMomentumScrollEnd` | A scroll after the release is momentum. So is a scroll with no pointer down: the wheel, the keyboard, or `scrollTo`.                                                                    |
| `onContentSizeChange`                          | Gets the width and height of the content, after mount and after each change.                                                                                                            |

The scroll ends at the browser's `scrollend` event. A browser without `scrollend` ends it 150 ms after the last scroll event.

`scrollEventThrottle` isn't needed: the browser already sends one scroll event per frame.

## Props

| Prop                                                             | On the web                                                                                                                       |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `horizontal`                                                     | Scrolls on the x axis.                                                                                                           |
| `contentContainerStyle`                                          | The style of the content `View`.                                                                                                 |
| `scrollEnabled`                                                  | `false` hides the overflow, so nothing scrolls.                                                                                  |
| `contentOffset`                                                  | Sets the scroll position on mount, and again when it changes.                                                                    |
| `centerContent`                                                  | Centers content that is smaller than the box.                                                                                    |
| `snapToInterval`, `snapToOffsets`, `pagingEnabled`               | Snap after the scroll settles, with a smooth scroll. The scroll is instant when the user asks for reduced motion.                |
| `snapToAlignment`, `snapToStart`, `snapToEnd`                    | As on native. `snapToStart` and `snapToEnd` apply to `snapToOffsets`.                                                            |
| `showsVerticalScrollIndicator`, `showsHorizontalScrollIndicator` | `false` on the scroll axis hides the scrollbar.                                                                                  |
| `stickyHeaderIndices`                                            | Those children stick to the top. Vertical only, as on native.                                                                    |
| `stickyHeaderHiddenOnScroll`                                     | The sticky header slides out on a scroll down and comes back on a scroll up.                                                     |
| `invertStickyHeaders`                                            | The headers stick to the bottom.                                                                                                 |
| `keyboardDismissMode`                                            | `on-drag` blurs the focused field when a drag starts. `interactive` has no web effect.                                           |
| `refreshControl`                                                 | Wraps the scroller, so the control can own the pull gesture. `RefreshControl` itself isn't in the package yet, so pass your own. |
| View props                                                       | As on [`View`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/view).                                                                                                           |

These native-only props are accepted and ignored: `bounces`, `alwaysBounceHorizontal`, `alwaysBounceVertical`, `contentInset`, `contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior`, `decelerationRate`, `directionalLockEnabled`, `disableIntervalMomentum`, `indicatorStyle`, `keyboardShouldPersistTaps`, `maintainVisibleContentPosition`, `nestedScrollEnabled`, `overScrollMode`, `scrollsToTop`, the zoom props, and the other iOS and Android props.

## Ref

The ref is the scroll element with the React Native methods added:

| Method                                                                | On the web                                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scrollTo({ x, y, animated })`                                        | As on native. `animated` defaults to `true`. The DOM forms `scrollTo(x, y)` and `scrollTo({ left, top })` work too. |
| `scrollToEnd({ animated })`                                           | Scrolls to the end of the content.                                                                                  |
| `getScrollableNode()`, `getNativeScrollRef()`, `getScrollResponder()` | The scroll element.                                                                                                 |
| `getInnerViewNode()`                                                  | The content element.                                                                                                |
| `flashScrollIndicators()`                                             | Does nothing. The browser has no API for it.                                                                        |

The old positional form `scrollTo(y, x)` doesn't work, because the DOM `scrollTo(x, y)` takes the same arguments in the other order.

---

# `FlatList`

A list on top of [`ScrollView`](https://rootnative.github.io/web/scrollview), with the React Native `FlatList` API.

```tsx
import { FlatList, Text } from 'react-native'

export function Contacts({ contacts }) {
  return (
    <FlatList
      data={contacts}
      keyExtractor={(contact) => contact.id}
      renderItem={({ item }) => <Text>{item.name}</Text>}
      onEndReached={loadMore}
    />
  )
}
```

> **WARNING: No virtualizer yet**
>
> `FlatList` renders every item, so each one costs DOM memory and render time. Load a long list in pages with `onEndReached`.

Each item sits in a cell `View`, with its separator after it, as on native. The default `keyExtractor` uses `key`, then `id`, then the index, as on native.

## Props

| Prop                                                               | On the web                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `data`, `renderItem`, `ListItemComponent`, `keyExtractor`          | As on native.                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `ItemSeparatorComponent`                                           | Gets `highlighted` and `leadingItem`. `separators.highlight()`, `unhighlight()`, and `updateProps()` in `renderItem` work.                                                                                                          |
